title: Quickstart Templates — Metrics Mapping Sheet (Dashboards + Alerts)
body:
Context
- Purpose: map the metrics emitted by Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) to (a) Redwood Console views and (b) prebuilt dashboards + recommended alerts shipped via observability-pack.
- This is a spreadsheet-style working doc. Final metric list should remain stable across Python + TypeScript templates.
- Design goals:
  1) Supportability: enough signals to debug latency/cost/tool failures/retrieval issues.
  2) Low maintenance: minimal required config; safe defaults for local + prod.
  3) Low cardinality by default.

Naming / conventions (summary)
- Metrics are emitted as OpenTelemetry metrics with the following naming:
  - Core request metrics: redwood.quickstart.*
  - RAG/retrieval: redwood.quickstart.rag.*
  - Agents/tool calling: redwood.quickstart.agent.*
  - Networking/retries/streaming: redwood.quickstart.net.*
  - Evals/smoke tests (CI only): redwood.quickstart.eval.*
- Metric types: counter, histogram, gauge (only when needed).
- Units:
  - seconds for durations (OTel convention)
  - tokens as {token}
  - USD as {usd} (note: optional / estimated; may be derived in Console)
- Required resource attributes (stable, low-card):
  - service.name (template app name)
  - deployment.environment (local|staging|prod)
  - service.version (template version stamp)
- Required metric attributes (stable, low-card):
  - redwood.template (e.g., rag-agent)
  - redwood.template.language (python|typescript)
  - redwood.deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private) (optional; only if known)
  - redwood.model (pinned model id / alias) (keep limited; do NOT include full provider model string if it includes version hashes)
  - redwood.region (if available; keep to known region enum)
  - http.route (ONLY for small enumerated routes in template server; avoid raw URL path)
  - error.type (from template error taxonomy: auth|quota|network|timeout|tool|retrieval|parse|unknown)

Attributes to avoid (cardinality / privacy)
- DO NOT emit: user_id, email, account_id, raw prompt, raw completion, document text, query text.
- Avoid high-cardinality tags on metrics:
  - http.url, full path, request_id, trace_id
  - tool.name (unless small enumerated set defined in code)
  - vector.index_name (unless small enumerated set)
- If request correlation needed, use logs/traces (not metrics). Request IDs are OK in logs/traces with redaction rules.

Dashboards referenced
- D1: Quickstart Overview (traffic, success rate, p95 latency, tokens)
- D2: RAG Retrieval Health (retrieval latency, empty results rate, index errors)
- D3: Agent + Tools (tool call rate, tool failure rate, agent iterations)
- D4: Streaming Stability (disconnect rate, reconnect attempts)
- D5: Token Economics (tokens/request, tokens/sec, cache hit rate)

Recommended alerts (examples)
- A1: Error rate high (5xx or error.type != none)
- A2: p95 latency regression (request or generation)
- A3: Quota/rate-limit spikes (429)
- A4: Streaming disconnect spike
- A5: Retrieval empty results spike
- A6: Tool failure spike

---
TABLE (TSV)
Category	Metric name	Type	Unit	Description	Primary dashboard	Suggested alert	Required attributes	Allowed/optional attributes	Cardinality risk	Redaction/privacy note	Source / how emitted	Notes
Core	redwood.quickstart.request.count	counter	{request}	Count of template app requests (logical user requests)	D1	A1 (error rate derived)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; http.route	redwood.region; redwood.deployment_mode; redwood.model	LOW	No PII in attrs	Increment once per inbound request	If template is a web server, define explicit routes: /chat, /rag, /health
Core	redwood.quickstart.request.duration	histogram	seconds	End-to-end request duration (from inbound request to response complete)	D1	A2 (p95)	(same as above)	error.type (only when error)	MED	No raw URLs	Measured around handler; include streaming completion	For streaming, measure until stream closed; record error.type when disconnected
Core	redwood.quickstart.request.in_flight	gauge	{request}	Concurrent in-flight requests in the app	D1	(optional saturation alert)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language		LOW	N/A	Up/down around handler	Useful to correlate 429s with local saturation
Core	redwood.quickstart.response.status.count	counter	{response}	HTTP response status counts from template server	D1	A1	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; http.route	http.status_code (bucketed: 2xx|4xx|5xx)	LOW	Avoid emitting raw status code if it varies; use buckets	From response middleware	If using buckets, implement mapping 200-299 => 2xx, etc.
Core	redwood.quickstart.error.count	counter	{error}	Count of handled errors by taxonomy	D1	A1	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	error.type; error.retryable (true|false)	LOW	Do not include exception message	Increment where error is classified	Keep error.type aligned to template-error-taxonomy-draft

LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.request.duration	histogram	seconds	Duration of upstream LLM call (API request to first/last token; see attrs)	D1,D5	A2 (p95)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; redwood.model	llm.phase (ttfb|stream|total)	LOW	No prompts in attrs	Wrap Redwood SDK call; record phase metrics	If only one metric: llm.phase=total; optionally add ttfb
LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.tokens.prompt	histogram	{token}	Prompt tokens per request (from API usage)	D5	(optional cost spike)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; redwood.model	req.kind (rag|agent|chat)	LOW	No content	From Redwood response usage	Histogram preferred over gauge to compute p95
LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.tokens.completion	histogram	{token}	Completion tokens per request	D5	(optional cost spike)	(same as above)	req.kind	LOW	No content	From Redwood response usage	Used for tokens/request and cost estimation
LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.tokens.total	histogram	{token}	Total tokens per request	D5	(optional)	(same as above)	req.kind	LOW	No content	Derived or direct	If emitting prompt+completion, total can be derived; keep if it simplifies dashboards
LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.cache.hit.count	counter	{hit}	Count of requests served with cache assist (prefix/KV/prompt cache when available)	D5	(optional: cache drop)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; redwood.model	cache.type (prefix|kv|prompt); cache.hit (true|false)	LOW	No content	From SDK headers/metadata when supported	If cache metadata not available in all modes, treat as optional
LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.rate_limited.count	counter	{event}	Count of upstream 429 responses from Redwood API	D1	A3	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	error.type=quota	LOW	No customer identifiers	Increment on 429 classification	Also log retry-after and guidance (in logs)
LLM	redwood.quickstart.llm.auth_failed.count	counter	{event}	Count of upstream auth failures (401/403)	D1	A1 (auth)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	error.type=auth	LOW	No key material	Increment on 401/403 classification	Useful for “API key missing/invalid” onboarding issues

Networking	redwood.quickstart.net.retry.attempts	histogram	{attempt}	Retries attempted per upstream call	D1	(optional: retry spike)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	retry.reason (timeout|reset|429|5xx|unknown)	LOW	No URLs	From retry wrapper/middleware	Histogram captures distribution; also consider counter for total attempts
Networking	redwood.quickstart.net.timeout.count	counter	{event}	Number of timeout events (upstream or downstream)	D1	A2/A1	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	error.type=timeout; net.peer.name (ENUM ONLY)	MED	Avoid raw hostnames	Increment when timeout exception classified	If net.peer.name varies (customer proxies), remove it
Streaming	redwood.quickstart.stream.disconnect.count	counter	{event}	Count of client stream disconnects (broken pipe / canceled)	D4	A4	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	stream.side (client|upstream)	LOW	No client identifiers	Emit when stream ends unexpectedly	Differentiate client cancel vs upstream drop if possible
Streaming	redwood.quickstart.stream.reconnect.count	counter	{event}	Count of reconnect attempts performed by the template/SDK	D4	A4	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	reconnect.outcome (success|fail)	LOW	No request_id in attrs	Emit from reconnect logic	Only for SDKs that support reconnect; optional in Python if not implemented

RAG	redwood.quickstart.rag.retrieval.duration	histogram	seconds	Time spent retrieving documents (vector db/query + post-filter)	D2	A2	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	retriever.type (local|hosted|custom)	LOW	No query text	Wrap retriever call	If hosted vector DB vendor varies, keep retriever.type coarse
RAG	redwood.quickstart.rag.retrieval.results	histogram	{document}	Number of documents returned by retriever	D2	A5	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	retriever.type	LOW	No doc ids	Emit after retrieval	Used to compute “empty results rate” (results==0)
RAG	redwood.quickstart.rag.retrieval.empty.count	counter	{event}	Count of retrievals returning 0 results	D2	A5	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	retriever.type	LOW	No query text	Increment when results==0	Alert should consider baseline (some queries legitimately empty)
RAG	redwood.quickstart.rag.context.tokens	histogram	{token}	Estimated tokens for retrieved context sent to LLM	D5	(optional cost cap)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; redwood.model	req.kind=rag	LOW	No content	Compute via tokenizer when available	If tokenizer dependency is heavy, make optional; cost control still works via character count
RAG	redwood.quickstart.rag.indexing.duration	histogram	seconds	Time spent indexing/ingesting documents (offline or startup)	D2	(optional)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	indexer.phase (chunk|embed|upsert)	LOW	No document text	Emit during ingestion command	Not emitted during normal request path
RAG	redwood.quickstart.rag.indexing.error.count	counter	{error}	Indexing/ingestion failures	D2	(optional)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	error.type=retrieval; indexer.phase	LOW	No filenames if user-specific	Increment on ingestion error	Log full stack in debug logs only (with redaction)

Agent	redwood.quickstart.agent.iterations	histogram	{iteration}	Number of agent loop iterations per request	D3	(optional runaway)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language; redwood.model	agent.outcome (success|max_iter|error)	LOW	No prompt content	Emit at end of agent run	Correlate with cost and tool failures
Agent	redwood.quickstart.agent.tool.calls	counter	{call}	Total tool invocations	D3	A6	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	tool.name (ENUM ONLY); tool.outcome (success|error|timeout|validation)	MED	Tool arguments MUST NOT be attrs	Emit when tool executed	If tool.name is user-defined/free-form, remove tool.name or map to “custom_tool”
Agent	redwood.quickstart.agent.tool.duration	histogram	seconds	Tool execution duration	D3	A6	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	tool.name (ENUM ONLY); tool.outcome	MED	No args	Wrap tool call	Same cardinality caveat as tool.calls
Agent	redwood.quickstart.agent.tool.validation_failed.count	counter	{event}	Count of tool schema validation failures	D3	A6	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	error.type=tool	LOW	No tool payloads	Emit when tool output/args fail schema validation	Maps to common ticket: tool schema parse error
Agent	redwood.quickstart.agent.tool.output_truncated.count	counter	{event}	Count of times tool output exceeded limit and was truncated	D3	(optional)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	tool.name (ENUM ONLY)	MED	Do not emit output length if it encodes sensitive sizes? OK as numeric only	Emit when enforcing tool output cap	Helps tune safe defaults; careful with tool.name cardinality

Adoption tagging (metric-level signals optional)	redwood.quickstart.template.tagged_request.count	counter	{request}	Count of requests with template-origin tag/header successfully attached	D1	(optional instrumentation health)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	tag.transport (header|metadata)	LOW	No user identifiers	Increment when tag applied	Telemetry tags must be opt-in if proxy/header issues persist

Collector/export health	redwood.quickstart.otel.export.error.count	counter	{event}	Errors exporting spans/metrics to collector/exporter	D1	(optional)	service.name; deployment.environment; service.version; redwood.template; redwood.template.language	exporter.kind (otlphttp|otlpgRPC)	LOW	No endpoints in attrs	From OTel SDK error handler	Matches support ticket: exporter auth failing; logs should include actionable hint (without secrets)

---
Notes / open questions
1) Do we emit cost in metrics?
   - Proposal: do NOT emit usd by default to avoid confusion and pricing drift. Dashboards can compute cost in Console using usage + price tables.
   - Optional metric (if needed for non-Console users): redwood.quickstart.llm.cost.estimated (histogram {usd}) computed from response usage and a static price map pinned to template version.

2) http.status_code dimension
   - Prefer bucketed status_class to keep cardinality low.

3) Model naming
   - Use Redwood model alias (e.g., redwood.model=rw:llama-3.1-70b-instruct) rather than provider-native full ids. This also reduces churn.

4) RAG retriever/tool naming
   - Biggest cardinality risk in agents is tool.name; biggest in RAG is retriever index name/vendor. We should keep these coarse (local|hosted|custom) unless we can guarantee enumerated sets.

5) Required vs optional metrics
   - Required for v1 template launch: request.count, request.duration, error.count, llm.request.duration, llm.tokens.(prompt|completion), stream.disconnect.count, rag.retrieval.duration, rag.retrieval.empty.count, agent.tool.calls, agent.tool.validation_failed.count.
   - Optional for post-launch: cache metrics, export health, indexing metrics, reconnect metrics (depends on SDK).

Change log
- 2025-02-03: Added streaming stability metrics + suggested A4.
- 2025-02-14: Added agent tool schema validation metric for common failure mode.
- 2025-02-26: Tightened guidance on avoiding tool.name high cardinality; added “ENUM ONLY” rule.
- 2025-03-04: Added otel export health metric mapping to SUP-29422 class of issues; marked telemetry-tagged requests as opt-in dependent.
